Buying a new Mississauga condo? Check 4 things before you sign. 1) Review the disclosure statement and buyer's guide with your real estate lawyer. 2) New condos have a 10-day cooling-off period that begins after you receive the required documents. 3) Builders must hold condo deposits in trust; Tarion protects up to $20,000. 4) Read the Statement of Critical Dates and the cancellation conditions closely.

Send this to someone buying a new condo. (Sources: Condo Authority of Ontario, Pre-construction condos; Tarion, deposit protection; accessed Oct 2026.) Rules and eligibility apply. General information only, not legal advice.

Condo or townhouse in Milton? Compare these 4 costs. 1) Condo fees: set by the condo corporation, so ask what they cover. 2) Property tax: based on the home's assessed value; ask for the latest bill. 3) Utilities: see which are in the fee and which are yours. 4) Insurance: condo and freehold policies differ, so get a quote first.

General information only, not tax, mortgage or legal advice.

A Caledon buyer asked me: what happens to my deposit? 1) In a typical resale, your deposit is held in trust. 2) At closing, it is credited toward your purchase price. 3) If a deal ends early, your agreement and your lawyer decide what happens. Save this before you make an offer.

General information only, not legal advice.

Final walkthrough in Kitchener? Check these 4 things first. 1) Test the lights, taps, outlets and appliances included in your deal. 2) Check windows, doors and walls for new damage since your inspection. 3) Confirm every included item is still there and the sellers' belongings are gone. 4) Found a problem? Tell your real estate lawyer right away, before closing.
